officialTitle: Extra-pleural pneumonectomy versus no extra-pleural pneumonectomy for patients with malignant pleural mesothelioma: clinical outcomes of the Mesothelioma and Radical Surgery (MARS) randomised feasibility study
setting: Trimodality therapy for operable pleural mesothelioma

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between Oct 1, 2005, and Nov 3, 2008, 112 patients were registered and 50 were subsequently randomly assigned: 24 to EPP and 26 to no EPP.
design.notes: Randomised feasibility study at 12 UK hospitals. All patients had induction platinum-based chemotherapy before randomisation to extrapleural pneumonectomy followed by hemithorax irradiation versus no EPP. Not powered for survival; recorded as phase II for feasibility design (phase not stated in abstract).

clinicalQuestion: Is it feasible to randomise patients to extrapleural pneumonectomy within trimodality therapy, and what are the clinical outcomes compared with no EPP?

pico.population: Pathologically confirmed pleural mesothelioma fit for trimodality therapy after induction platinum-based chemotherapy
pico.intervention: Extrapleural pneumonectomy followed by postoperative hemithorax irradiation
pico.outcomes: Feasibility, perioperative mortality, overall survival, quality of life

arms.label: EPP
arms.regimen: Induction platinum chemotherapy, then extrapleural pneumonectomy and hemithorax radiotherapy

arms.label: No EPP
arms.regimen: Induction platinum chemotherapy, no extrapleural pneumonectomy

publications.title: Extra-pleural pneumonectomy versus no extra-pleural pneumonectomy for patients with malignant pleural mesothelioma: clinical outcomes of the Mesothelioma and Radical Surgery (MARS) randomised feasibility study.
publications.label: Principal clinical outcomes report

outcomes.sourceQuote: The hazard ratio [HR] for overall survival between the EPP and no EPP groups was 1·90 (95% CI 0·92-3·93; exact p=0·082), and after adjustment for sex, histological subtype, stage, and age at randomisation the HR was 2·75 (1·21-6·26; p=0·016). Median survival was 14·4 months (5·3-18·7) for the EPP group and 19·5 months (13·4 to time not yet reached) for the no EPP group.

outcomes.population: ITT, adjusted for sex, histological subtype, stage and age
outcomes.sourceQuote: after adjustment for sex, histological subtype, stage, and age at randomisation the HR was 2·75 (1·21-6·26; p=0·016).

safety.sourceQuote: There were ten serious adverse events reported in the EPP group and two in the no EPP group.

safety.description: Perioperative deaths in the EPP group
safety.sourceQuote: Two patients in the EPP group died within 30 days and a further patient died without leaving hospital.

strengths: Only randomised evaluation of extrapleural pneumonectomy
limitations: Feasibility study with small sample; not powered for survival
Many registered patients did not proceed to randomisation
EPP not completed in a substantial proportion of those allocated

clinicalImplications.text: The authors concluded that extrapleural pneumonectomy within trimodality therapy offered no benefit and possibly harmed patients, and that a larger trial was not feasible; this contributed to a move away from EPP.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Randomised data, although small, do not support extrapleural pneumonectomy; morbidity and perioperative mortality were substantial.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 21723781. Feasibility results are detailed in another report not ingested.
